These choroidal changes during refractive error development occur rapidly^[@CR3]^ and are typically found to precede changes in scleral growth^[@CR4]^. Stimuli that typically slow eye growth in the longer term (and result in the development of hyperopic refractive errors) are associated with a thickening of the choroid, whereas stimuli that result in the more rapid eye growth (and result in the development of myopia in the longer term) are typically associated with a thinning of the choroid^[@CR5]^. Similar to a range of animal models studied so far; human studies have also shown an association between changes in refractive error and alterations in subfoveal choroidal thickness. texts.full_text: Burma: The University of Michigan has substantial investments in corporations that do business with Burma. Thanks to the efforts of the Environmental Justice Group, the Michigan Student Assembly voted to encourage the Regents to divest from Burma. Other goals included:: 1) lobbying the Regents and elected officials to implement this policy, and 2) encouraging Professor Marina Whitman, a board member of Unocal, to encourage that company to withdraw from its pipeline project in Burma. Hamtramck Environmental Action Team: This team campaigned to pressure Michigan Waste Services to apply cleaner technologies and to discontinue non-essential medicawaste dumping on Hamtrack city streets during the night shift collection routes.: The group also worked with local officials, organized public forums for community education about environmental issues in their area of residence; they even created an educational video documentary detailing these problems which was shown at schools throughout Detroit as well! The Environmental Justice Group and Michigan Student Assembly's efforts to encourage divestment from Burma are commendable. By lobbying the Regents on this issue while also targeting Professor Marina Whitman, who sits both academically prestigiously within U-M circles but more importantly holds influence over Unocal’s decisions regarding their pipeline project there too - they've taken proactive steps towards achieving social responsibility goals

texts.full_text: middle of the text, the author, Mark Safranski, begins by stating that he often reviews good books and sometimes reviews great ones. He then introduces the book "The Rule of the Clan" by Mark Weiner, which he reviews. Safranski praises Weiner's work for its ability to combine academic rigor with accessibility and insight. He notes that Weiner, a Professor of Law and Sidney I. Reitman Scholar at Rutgers University, has focused on the evolution of constitutional orders and legal anthropology. Safranski highlights Weiner's exploration of the historical hypothesis of tension between ancient forms of social organization and the future of individual freedom. He concludes by stating that Weiner has effectively laid out a hypothesis that examines the constitutional nature of a global phenomenon that has plagued IR scholars, COIN theorists, diplomats, counterterrorism experts, unconventional warfare officers, strategists, politicians, and judges. Weiner has put his talents to use in examining the constitutional nature of a global phenomena that has plagued IR scholars, COIN theorists, diplomats, counterterrorism experts, unconventional warfare officers, strategists, politicians and judges. texts.full_text: rger codebase using PyQt4 for networking operations and intersphinx inventory reading for documentation purposes. To complete the `search` method in your `HelpProvider` class, you need to specify what kind of search functionality you want to implement. Here's a basic example of how you might start implementing a search function that leverages the QNetworkAccessManager for making network requests: ```python class HelpProvider(QObject): def __init__(self, parent=None): QObject.__init__(self, parent) self.manager = QNetworkAccessManager(self) def search(self, query, url): request = QNetworkRequest(QUrl(url)) reply = self.manager.get(request) # You would typically connect signals and slots to handle the response # For example, you might want to process the data in a slot when the reply is finished. reply.finished.connect(self.on_reply_finished) def on_reply_finished(self): reply = self.sender() if reply.error() != QNetworkReply.NoError: log.error(f"Request failed: {reply.errorString()}") else: data = reply.readAll() # Process the data here as needed log.info(f"Data received: {data}") # Cleanup reply.deleteLater() # Example usage: # help_provider = HelpProvider() # help_provider.search("example query", "http://example.com/search") ``` This example provides a basic structure for initiating a search request and handling the response. The `search` method sends a GET request to the specified URL, and the `on_reply_finished` method processes the reply when it's completed. You would need to extend this example to fit your specific requirements, such as parsing the data received from the server and displaying search results in a user-friendly way.
